summary.headline: LTM to acquire Randstad's Europe and Australia tech and consulting arm: €469M revenue, €160M EV, plus a five-year Randstad GCC deal worth ~$55–60M initial scope.
summary.overview: LTM announced on May 22, 2026 a proposed acquisition of Randstad's Technology and Consulting Services business in Europe and Australia, with annualized revenue of €469M (about $500M+) and a proposed enterprise value of €160M on a cash-free, debt-free basis. The package has three parts: the acquisition, a five-year IT services partnership to scale Randstad's GCC in Hyderabad with an AI-centric approach, and an agreement for LTM to manage subcontractor spend through Randstad's MSP capabilities. Management said the asset is a white-space play in continental Europe, Australia, and the aerospace & defence, automotive, utilities and BFS verticals, and will be run as a separate subsidiary. The call was Q&A-heavy on revenue decline, margin dilution, and the durability of client relationships; the transcript contains no reported Q4 FY26 financials.

segments.name: Randstad Technology & Consulting (target)
segments.commentary: €469M annualized revenue, 78% Europe and 22% Australia; 15+ scaled accounts; capabilities in digital engineering, cybersecurity, industrial IoT, and security-cleared talent for aerospace & defence.

segments.name: Randstad GCC partnership (Hyderabad)
segments.commentary: Five-year IT services deal to scale Randstad's GCC with AI-centric transformation; initial scope ramp of ~$55–60M TCV, with LTM as preferred partner.

segments.name: Subcontractor management
segments.commentary: Five-year arrangement to use Randstad Group's MSP capabilities to manage LTM subcontractors, with contracted savings; no financial size disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Management expects no material impact on EBIT margin in the year of closing or the following year, supported by GCC scaling, subcon savings and onsite margins above LTM's.
Amortization impact described as not very material; management said no EPS dilution is expected if margin impact is absent.
Management expects a further haircut in the short term from trimming tail accounts, possibly around 10 more accounts, but targets doubling revenue over five years via cross-sell and upsell.
Investment in sales is described as minimal, mainly a separate overlay sales team for LTM service lines.
Deal closing is the current focus; revenue-synergy timing and large-deal pipeline details deferred to future quarterly commentary and the investor day.
capex_capacity: Target adds delivery centres in Romania and Portugal to existing Poland nearshore capacity.
Offshore capacity gap: target had limited offshore scale; LTM expects to add offshore rate cards and offshore MSAs/SOWs into existing contracts in some accounts.
Post-deal, LTM's total workforce is close to 87,000 people, which management cited as a cross-sell channel.
Target to be run as a standalone subsidiary with only functional integration (finance, HR); no operational integration planned.
demand_pricing: Revenue decline attributed to three causes: European macro weakness, a deliberate tail-account trim in FY2025 ahead of the divestment, and clients ramping their own GCCs with target lacking scale offshore.
Target's commercial mix is T&M, fixed price, managed services and solutions; average consultant tenure in accounts exceeds five years, with some consultants at seven to eight years.

Target accounts are described as white space for LTM with no current presence; verticals include aerospace & defence, automotive, utilities, telecom and BFS (two of top four Australian banks, top three French banks).
Target's onsite gross margin is described as better than LTM's onsite gross margin; management did not give numbers.
DSO profile described as in line with LTM's own and typical for IT services.

qa_highlights.question: Why has revenue declined about 10%, and can it be reversed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited European macro weakness, a FY2025 tail-account trim before divestment, and target clients moving work to their own GCCs; it said a year earlier the decline could have been arrested.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin implications and amortization cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Vipul Chandra said target onsite gross margins are good and LTM's offshore model can lift them; Venu Lambu said no material EBIT impact this year or next, and amortization is not expected to be very material.

qa_highlights.question: Why exclude Randstad's US business, and will the target grow at company rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said US overlap would be high and US was not white space. It expects a short-term haircut from tail trimming, but its plan rests on growing marquee accounts.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a conflict with group company LTTS?
qa_highlights.answer: Venu Lambu said there is no conflict with group companies; the target's capabilities are complementary to iNxt and the enterprise platforms.

qa_highlights.question: Will sales and marketing investment be needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Vipul Chandra said investment is minimal: the target brings sales staff with deep client relationships, and LTM will set up a separate overlay sales team.

qa_highlights.question: Is the deal EPS-accretive from day one, and what is the DSO profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Vipul Chandra said no margin impact means no EPS dilution; DSO is in line with LTM's and typical for IT services.

qa_highlights.question: How does the GCC partnership start, and what is the revenue scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Venu Lambu said the initial ramp scope is about $55–60M TCV within a five-year relationship; the deal grew out of a Board-level relationship.

qa_highlights.question: Is the use of cash justified, and does it come at the cost of capability build?
qa_highlights.answer: Vipul Chandra said consideration is 10–15% of LTM's cash, and Venu Lambu said capability investment continues alongside the deal.

risks_watch: Revenue trajectory: management expects further tail-account trimming in the short term, so target growth may lag LTM's guided mid-to-high single-digit rate.
Margin dilution: management says no material EBIT impact, but the target's offshore mix is low and the plan relies on the GCC ramp and subcon savings, not yet quantified.
Client-relationship risk: top 25 accounts are 65% of Europe revenue and top 10 are 80% of Australia revenue; T&M consultants are client-controlled, and knowledge transfer is unproven.
Integration and separate-subsidiary execution, including functional integration (finance, HR) and overlay sales build-out.
Closing timing and regulatory approvals, not discussed in the call; the consideration is cash-free, debt-free but the closing date and final terms were not given.
Scope of the Randstad GCC partnership beyond the initial $55–60M TCV, and whether Randstad's wider US/UK business is retained or divested, remain unclear.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on strategic fit and white-space logic. Evasive on the target's revenue trajectory, the reasons for the US carve-out, and the Randstad US/UK business plans, deferring detail until after closing.
key_quotes: The technology and consulting services business across these two big markets comes to annualized revenue of €469 million and we have a proposed enterprise value of €160 million on a cash free, debt free basis.
there is going to be no material impact to the margin, for this year, even after closure and for the next year, we have plan in place to make sure that there is no material impact.
In Europe, the top 25 customers contribute 65% of the revenue. In Australia, top 10 customers contribute to 80% of the revenue.
I would assume a little bit more haircut in the short term just to transform, the scaled accounts, I mean, these are marquee accounts.
